HOLD HARMLESS AND INDEMNITY AGREEMENT

THIS HOLD HARMLESS AND INDEMNITY AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is made as of March 30, 2026, by SUMMIT LEDGE CLIMBING COLLECTIVE, an Idaho nonprofit corporation ("Indemnitor"), in favor of PANHANDLE TIMBER HOLDINGS LLC, an Idaho limited liability company, and its members, managers, employees, agents, and affiliates (collectively, "Indemnitee").

RECITALS

A. Indemnitee owns approximately 1,840 acres of timberland in Bonner County, Idaho, including the granite formations locally known as the Selkirk Slabs (the "Property").

B. Indemnitor wishes to conduct guided rock-climbing instruction and organized climbing events on the Property, and Indemnitee is willing to permit that use in exchange for the indemnity below.

NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, Indemnitor agrees as follows.

1. Permitted Use.

Indemnitee grants Indemnitor a revocable, non-exclusive license to enter the Property for guided rock-climbing instruction and organized climbing events, during daylight hours, on the routes shown on Exhibit A. This license is not a lease, conveys no interest in land, and may be revoked by Indemnitee at any time on written notice.

2. Indemnity.

Indemnitor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Indemnitee from and against any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, losses, damages, liabilities, judgments, settlements, fines, penalties, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees and expert fees, arising out of or relating to (a) Indemnitor's use of the Property, (b) the acts or omissions of Indemnitor, its officers, employees, volunteers, instructors, participants, and guests, and (c) any breach by Indemnitor of this Agreement, in each case regardless of whether the claim is caused in whole or in part by the negligence of Indemnitee, but excluding any claim to the extent caused by Indemnitee's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

3. Idaho Anti-Indemnity Limitation.

Idaho Code § 29-114 makes void and unenforceable a provision in a construction agreement that purports to indemnify a party against liability for damages caused by that party's own negligence. This Agreement is not a construction agreement and Section 2 is not intended to reach conduct that statute protects; if a court determines that any portion of Section 2 is void under § 29-114 or any comparable statute, that portion is severed and the remainder of Section 2 is enforced to the fullest extent the law permits, including as an indemnity for the negligence of Indemnitor alone.

4. Defense and Cooperation.

Indemnitee shall give Indemnitor written notice of any claim for which it seeks indemnity promptly after Indemnitee becomes aware of it, and a delay in giving notice relieves Indemnitor only to the extent Indemnitor is actually and materially prejudiced. Indemnitor shall assume the defense with counsel reasonably satisfactory to Indemnitee. Indemnitee may participate at its own expense, and may assume its own defense at Indemnitor's expense if Indemnitor fails to assume the defense within twenty (20) days after notice or if a conflict of interest makes joint representation improper. Indemnitor shall not settle any claim in a manner that imposes any liability, injunction, or admission of fault on Indemnitee without Indemnitee's prior written consent. Indemnitee shall cooperate reasonably in the defense at Indemnitor's expense.

5. No Cap.

The obligations of Indemnitor under this Agreement are not subject to any cap, deductible, retention, or aggregate limit, and are not reduced by the amount of any insurance available to Indemnitee.

6. Insurance.

Indemnitor shall maintain, at its own expense and for so long as this Agreement remains in effect and for three (3) years afterward, commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and $5,000,000 in the aggregate, together with participant accident coverage of not less than $100,000 per participant, each written on an occurrence basis by an insurer rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best. Indemnitee shall be named as an additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis, and each policy shall include a waiver of subrogation in Indemnitee's favor. Indemnitor shall furnish certificates and endorsements before first entry and on each renewal, and shall give Indemnitee thirty (30) days' written notice before any cancellation or material reduction.

7. Participant Releases.

Indemnitor shall obtain from every participant, before that participant enters the Property, a signed release and assumption of risk in a form Indemnitee approves in writing, naming Indemnitee as a released party, and shall retain those releases for four (4) years and produce them to Indemnitee on request.

8. Condition of the Property.

Indemnitee makes no representation or warranty as to the condition of the Property or the safety of any route, and Indemnitor accepts the Property "as is, where is, with all faults." Indemnitee has no duty to inspect, maintain, warn of, or repair any natural or artificial condition, and Indemnitor acknowledges that Idaho Code § 36-1604 limits a landowner's liability to recreational users.

9. Term and Survival.

This Agreement begins on the date first written above and continues until terminated by either party on thirty (30) days' written notice. Termination does not affect any obligation arising from conduct occurring before termination, and Sections 2 through 5 and Section 7 survive termination indefinitely.

10. Governing Law; Forum; Counterparts.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Idaho, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any proceeding shall be brought in the District Court of the First Judicial District of the State of Idaho, in and for Bonner County. This Agreement is the entire agreement of the parties concerning its subject matter, may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties, and may be executed in counterparts.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.
